newsitem.title: USA: American Air pilots board OKs contract proposal.
newsitem.headline: American Air pilots board OKs contract proposal.

text.p: Leaders of American Airlines pilots union Friday approved a proposed labour agreement with the nation's second largest air carrier, although the rank and file still had to vote on the pact.
The leaders of the Allied Pilots Association said they would ask their 9,300 members who work for American to vote on the proposal within six weeks.
Last fall APA members defied their leadership and voted to reject a proposed contract despite the union board's recommendation for approval.

The pilots, who briefly struck the airline in February before President Bill Clinton ordered them back to work, could strike within 30 days if they reject the latest offer from the airline, a unit of Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR Corp.
The union's 18-member board voted by a margin of 12 to six to approve the latest contract proposal, which was hammered out 16 days ago.
"Our position is the same as it was 10 days ago. There is no more to be gained by more negotiations," union President James Sovich told a news conference.
"We will now take steps to inform the membership of the terms of the agreement," Sovich said.

He said members of the negotiating committee and other APA officials planned to begin a two-week "road show" in Dallas to explain the terms of the agreement to the pilots. They will also visit eight other cities.

"If the membership is willing to strike over the regional jet issue, we will strike (against American Airlines)," he said. "These are educated adults. We'll just present them with the information in the contract."
The issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, was the major concern of most pilots.
American Airlines wants American Eagle pilots, who are paid less than APA members, to fly smaller jets so the company can remain competitive with low-cost commuter carriers.
The APA pilots are concerned that American Eagle pilots will eventually take over their current routes.

The proposed five-year agreement includes a 9 percent wage increase, a stock option programme and a guarantee that furloughed pilots will be tapped to fly new jets that the carrier is buying for American Eagle.
